sources.title: DDR Timing Closure: Physical Design and STA Methodology
sources.what_it_covers: A Corrent Corporation DDR interface implementation: timing constraints, timing-driven placement, clock-tree requirements, PrimeTime analysis, Tcl-based analysis, and post-layout ECOs. The authors explicitly report that conventional place-and-route approaches did not work and describe the methodology that achieved quick timing closure across multiple chips.
sources.why_relevant: Strong match for a verified physical-design closure story: a concrete high-speed ASIC interface, an implementation problem, corrective methodology, and closure outcome.

sources.title: Doing Your Due Diligence “Physically”
sources.what_it_covers: Kenneth Chang of iVivity describes physical-design evaluation and adoption for large SoCs, including multi-CPU block floorplan shrink and high-speed microprocessor-core evaluation, with quantitative area/timing results and decisions about hard versus soft macros.
sources.why_relevant: Useful physical-design war-story material: it documents real project uncertainty, vendor evaluation, floorplan resizing, timing concerns, and concrete changes that produced substantial die-area improvement while retaining timing closure.

sources.title: Case Study: First-Time Success ASIC Design Methodology Applied to a Multi-Processor System-on-Chip
sources.venue_or_publication: IntechOpen, Application Specific Integrated Circuits - Technologies, Digital Systems and Design Methodologies
sources.what_it_covers: The RUMPS401 four-core MPSoC implementation from specification through synthesis, floorplanning, power planning, placement, CTS, timing, IR-drop analysis, routing, post-layout simulation, tapeout, and first-silicon testing. It includes specific closure problems such as a Flash-output timing violation and a post-CTS hold violation, together with the fixes.
sources.why_relevant: One of the strongest public, end-to-end ASIC physical-design case studies: named chip, named implementation tools, numerical timing/IR-drop results, concrete violations, fixes, tapeout, and working first silicon.

sources.title: [OpenROAD] BoomTile/Megaboom: 20k routing congestion DRCs at only 0.24 placement density
sources.what_it_covers: A real OpenROAD physical-design failure involving severe routing congestion/DRCs despite very low reported placement density, with investigation of floorplan/routing-resource causes and attempted remedies in an open engineering discussion.
sources.why_relevant: Excellent failure-and-recovery forum source for the registry because the underlying artifacts, commands, tool versions, design, congestion observations, and debugging discussion are public and inspectable rather than being a generic tutorial.

sources.title: The](https://github.com/The-OpenROAD-Project/OpenROAD/issues/6066%22,%22access_guess%22:%22free%22},{%22title%22:%22The) chip met timing, and still failed signoff.
sources.what_it_covers: A representative digital-SoC implementation/signoff programme describing the failure mode where timing closure was achieved but signoff remained blocked by other physical constraints, including power, IR drop, antenna, corners, and physical verification.
sources.why_relevant: Directly relevant to a closure-failure registry because it frames the practical divergence between STA closure and complete physical/signoff closure and discusses the recovery workflow across signoff dimensions.

sources.title: PNR: A Complete 28nm Physical Design Case Study Using Synopsys ICC2
sources.venue_or_publication: Fusion of Multidisciplinary Research, Vol. 7, Issue 1
sources.what_it_covers: A full 28nm RTL-to-signoff physical-implementation case study using Synopsys ICC2, including floorplanning, congestion-aware placement, high-fanout-net synthesis, CTS, concurrent clock/data optimization, routing, timing closure, signal integrity, IR drop, and signoff metrics.
sources.why_relevant: Provides unusually explicit quantitative closure data and records how congestion, fanout, CTS, hold/setup timing, and extracted-parasitic effects interact during physical implementation.
